claim: The molecular underpinnings of synaptic vesicle fusion for fast neurotransmitter release are still unclear.
source: The molecular underpinnings of synaptic vesicle fusion for fast neurotransmitter release are still unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field, representing a gap in understanding.

claim: All instances of Ca2+-triggered immediate fusion started from a membrane–membrane point-contact and proceeded to complete fusion without discernible hemifusion intermediates.
source: Remarkably, all instances of Ca2+-triggered immediate fusion started from a membrane–membrane point-contact and proceeded to complete fusion without discernible hemifusion intermediates.
evidence: This claim is supported by single vesicle-vesicle microscopy experiments and cryo-EM imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pathways that involved a stable hemifusion diaphragm only resulted in fusion after many seconds, if at all.
source: In contrast, pathways that involved a stable hemifusion diaphragm only resulted in fusion after many seconds, if at all.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations from fluorescence intensity time traces shown in Figure 4B.

claim: When complexin was included, the Ca2+-triggered fusion network shifted towards the immediate pathway, effectively synchronizing fusion, especially at lower Ca2+-concentration.
source: When complexin was included, the Ca2+-triggered fusion network shifted towards the immediate pathway, effectively synchronizing fusion, especially at lower Ca2+-concentration.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6 comparing fusion with and without complexin.

claim: Synaptic proteins may have evolved to select the immediate pathway out of a heterogeneous network of possible membrane fusion pathways.
source: Synaptic proteins may have evolved to select this immediate pathway out of a heterogeneous network of possible membrane fusion pathways.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings regarding the role of synaptic proteins.

claim: Protein-mediated membrane fusion plays a key role in entry of enveloped viruses, fertilization, development, carcinogenesis, intracellular trafficking, secretion, and neurotransmitter release.
source: There are many examples where protein-mediated membrane fusion plays a key role, such as entry of enveloped viruses, fertilization, development, carcinogenesis, intracellular trafficking, secretion, and neurotransmitter release (Rothman, 1994; Jahn et al., 2003; Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Harrison, 2008; Rizo and Rosenmund, 2008; Moreau et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Synaptic vesicle fusion is unique in that it is both regulated and fast, in the order of a millisecond.
source: Among these biological processes, synaptic vesicle fusion is unique in that it is both regulated and fast, in the order of a millisecond (Meinrenken et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Upon an action potential, at most one synaptic vesicle undergoes exocytosis in a synapse among the readily releasable pool.
source: Upon an action potential, at most one synaptic vesicle undergoes exocytosis in a synapse among the readily releasable pool (Dobrunz and Stevens, 1997), that is, only a small subset of docked synaptic vesicles undergo fusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Protein-mediated fusion between biological membranes is thought to proceed from a pre-fusion contact to a fusion pore through one or more intermediates.
source: Protein-mediated fusion between biological membranes is thought to proceed from a pre-fusion contact to a fusion pore through one or more intermediates (Chernomordik and Kozlov, 2008; Jackson and Chapman, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A hemifusion intermediate is defined as a membrane state where the outer leaflets of the two juxtaposed membranes exchange lipids.
source: A hemifusion intermediate is defined as a membrane state where the outer leaflets of the two juxtaposed membranes exchange lipids; examples include an hourglass shaped 'stalk' and an elongated hemifusion diaphragm.
evidence: This is a definition based on established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Model calculations suggested that a hemifusion diaphragm is an energetically relatively stable, long-lived intermediate.
source: Model calculations suggested that a hemifusion diaphragm is an energetically relatively stable, long-lived intermediate, and that the direct pathway from stalk to fusion pore may be faster (Kuzmin et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior modeling work.

claim: The direct pathway from stalk to fusion pore may be faster than the classical pathway with a hemifusion diaphragm intermediate.
source: Model calculations suggested that a hemifusion diaphragm is an energetically relatively stable, long-lived intermediate, and that the direct pathway from stalk to fusion pore may be faster (Kuzmin et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior modeling work.

claim: Several key proteins cooperate in Ca2+-triggered synaptic vesicle fusion, including the soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptors (SNAREs), the Ca2+ sensor synaptotagmin 1, the activator/inhibitor complexin, and SM proteins.
source: Several key proteins cooperate in Ca2+-triggered synaptic vesicle fusion, including the soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptors (SNAREs) (Söllner et al., 1993; Sutton et al., 1998; Jahn and Scheller, 2006), the Ca2+ sensor synaptotagmin 1, the activator/inhibitor complexin, and SM proteins (Rizo and Rosenmund, 2008; Südhof and Rothman, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Exocytosis can proceed by full-collapse fusion, where the opening of a small pore continues to expand to a large pore.
source: Exocytosis can proceed by full-collapse fusion, where the opening of a small pore continues to expand to a large pore, and 'kiss-and-run', where a small pore opens transiently but closes again as the vesicle stays associated with the plasma membrane (Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Exocytosis can proceed by 'kiss-and-run', where a small pore opens transiently but closes again as the vesicle stays associated with the plasma membrane.
source: Exocytosis can proceed by full-collapse fusion, where the opening of a small pore continues to expand to a large pore, and 'kiss-and-run', where a small pore opens transiently but closes again as the vesicle stays associated with the plasma membrane (Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: SNARE proteins can promote membrane fusion via hemifusion intermediates, as inferred from lipid-mixing studies with proteoliposomes.
source: SNARE proteins can promote membrane fusion via hemifusion intermediates, as inferred from lipid-mixing studies with proteoliposomes where fluorescent labels measure the exchange of components between lipid bilayers (Weber et al., 1998; Reese and Mayer, 2005; Xu et al., 2005; Schaub et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior lipid-mixing studies.

claim: Content mixing is the correlate for neurotransmitter release.
source: However, it is content mixing, that is, the diffusion between compartments of small molecules with size comparable or slightly larger to that of neurotransmitter molecules that is the correlate for neurotransmitter release.
evidence: This is based on the understanding of what constitutes neurotransmitter release at a molecular level.

claim: Content mixing is not necessarily correlated with lipid mixing for biological membrane fusion.
source: Several previous studies implied that content mixing is not necessarily correlated with lipid mixing for biological membrane fusion: neuronal SNAREs alone do not produce much content mixing, although they readily induce lipid mixing (Bowen et al., 2004; Kyoung et al., 2011), influenza virus-induced fusion content mixing occurs seconds after initial lipid mixing (Floyd et al., 2008), and content mixing occurs with minutes delay after lipid mixing in vacuolar fusion (Jun and Wickner, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies showing discrepancies between lipid and content mixing.

claim: Neuronal SNAREs alone do not produce much content mixing, although they readily induce lipid mixing.
source: neuronal SNAREs alone do not produce much content mixing, although they readily induce lipid mixing (Bowen et al., 2004; Kyoung et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Influenza virus-induced fusion content mixing occurs seconds after initial lipid mixing.
source: influenza virus-induced fusion content mixing occurs seconds after initial lipid mixing (Floyd et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Content mixing occurs with minutes delay after lipid mixing in vacuolar fusion.
source: content mixing occurs with minutes delay after lipid mixing in vacuolar fusion (Jun and Wickner, 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Inner leaflet mixing can occur without content mixing when fusion is induced by DNA-zippering.
source: Even inner leaflet mixing can occur without content mixing when fusion is induced by DNA-zippering (Chan et al., 2009), although this intriguing observation will require verification with synaptic-protein induced fusion.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The single vesicle-vesicle system can discriminate between docking, hemifusion, and complete fusion.
source: Our system can discriminate between docking, hemifusion, and complete fusion.
evidence: This is a description of the capabilities of the experimental system developed by the authors.

claim: The improved system achieved a Ca2+ sensitivity in the 250–500 μM range.
source: After improvements in optical instrumentation as well as protein expression and purification, here we achieved a Ca2+ sensitivity in the 250–500 μM range.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from the improved system.

claim: The 250-500 μM Ca2+ range is reasonably close to the physiological concentration range (starting at 10 μM and saturating at several 100 μM).
source: This Ca2+ range is reasonably close to the physiological concentration range (starting at 10 μM and saturating at several 100 μM) (Heidelberger et al., 1994) and comparable to other recent in vitro experiments (Wang et al., 2011; Hernandez et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing physiological Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: The system mimics a stepwise Ca2+ concentration increase that acts on the readily-releasable pool of primed synaptic vesicles.
source: Our system mimics a stepwise Ca2+ concentration increase that acts on the readily-releasable pool of primed synaptic vesicles, and it is thus reminiscent to experiments with live neurons using photolysis of caged Ca2+ compounds (Schneggenburger and Neher, 2000; Sun et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system with citations to comparable in vivo experiments.

claim: A variety of morphologies of membrane-membrane interfaces were observed by cryo-EM, as well as changes in the distribution of membrane–membrane interfaces upon Ca2+ addition.
source: We observed a variety of morphologies of membrane-membrane interfaces, as well as changes in the distribution of membrane–membrane interfaces upon Ca2+ addition.
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM imaging data presented in Figure 2.

claim: All fast (immediate) fusion events start from a hemifusion-free state and proceed to full fusion upon Ca2+ injection without discernible hemifusion intermediates.
source: We found that all fast (immediate) fusion events start from a hemifusion-free state and proceed to full fusion upon Ca2+ injection without discernible hemifusion intermediates.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from single vesicle-vesicle microscopy shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Stable, initially hemifused states are slow to fuse, if at all.
source: In contrast, stable, initially hemifused states are slow to fuse, if at all.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from single vesicle-vesicle microscopy shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Complexin dramatically increases the number of immediate fusion events, with a more pronounced effect at lower Ca2+ concentration (250 μM).
source: Moreover, we found that complexin dramatically increases the number of immediate fusion events, with a more pronounced effect at lower Ca2+ concentration (250 μM).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Membrane compositions and protein number densities used mimic synaptic vesicles and the plasma membrane.
source: As before, we used membrane compositions and protein number densities that mimic synaptic vesicles and the plasma membrane, respectively
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design based on physiological parameters.

claim: The homogeneity of vesicle preparations was previously established.
source: We had previously established the homogeneity of our vesicle preparations (Kyoung et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The system started from a metastable state of docked vesicles at zero Ca2+ concentration after a defined incubation period.
source: After a defined incubation period our system started from a metastable state of docked vesicles at zero Ca2+ concentration.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: Upon Ca2+ injection, changes in membrane state were monitored in real-time by visual inspection of individual content and lipid mixing fluorescence intensity time traces.
source: Upon Ca2+ injection we monitored 'changes' in membrane state in real-time by visual inspection of individual content and lipid mixing fluorescence intensity time traces and identification of significant jumps in these traces.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methodology.

claim: Three characteristic changes in membrane state were observed: immediate fusion, delayed fusion, and hemifusion-only.
source: We observed three characteristic changes in membrane state, including instances of immediate fusion (a correlate with synchronous neurotransmitter release), delayed fusion (a correlate with asynchronous release), and hemifusion-only (i.e., without complete fusion) during the observation period of 50 s.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: For the minimal system consisting of only SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1, immediate fusion instances were in the minority.
source: Overall, for this very minimal system consisting of only SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1, immediate fusion instances were in the minority, followed by delayed fusion instances, and then hemifusion-only instances (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ca2+ triggered fusion depended on the presence of both functional SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1.
source: As we had shown previously, Ca2+ triggered fusion depended on the presence of both functional SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1, for example, mutation of one of the Ca2+ binding sites of synaptotagmin 1 greatly reduced the amount of immediate fusion and disruption of SNARE complex formation prevented both docking and fusion (Kyoung et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Many point contacts between donor and acceptor vesicles were observed before Ca2+ addition.
source: Many 'point contacts' (see 'Materials and methods' for definitions of all contact and interface types) between donor and acceptor vesicles were observed before Ca2+ addition (Figure 2B), as well as hemifusion diaphragms (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Hemifusion diaphragms were observed before Ca2+ addition.
source: Many 'point contacts' (see 'Materials and methods' for definitions of all contact and interface types) between donor and acceptor vesicles were observed before Ca2+ addition (Figure 2B), as well as hemifusion diaphragms (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Point contacts and hemifusion diaphragms are likely between donor and acceptor vesicles since no pronounced interactions between vesicles of the same type were observed in previous cryo-EM experiments.
source: Both point contacts and hemifusion diaphragms are likely between donor and acceptor vesicles since we did not observe interactions between vesicles of the same type in previous cryo-EM experiments (Kyoung et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on prior experimental observations cited.

claim: After Ca2+ addition, point contacts, hemifusion diaphragms, and extended close contacts without hemifusion were observed.
source: After Ca2+ addition, besides point contacts and hemifusion diaphragms (Figure 2D,E), we also observed a smaller number of 'extended' close contacts without hemifusion, defined as a triple-layered feature extending over more than 10 nm in length (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Similar extended close contacts were induced between liposomes by denatured Munc18.
source: Interestingly, similar extended close contacts were induced between liposomes by denatured Munc18 (Xu et al., 2011), and by SNAREs alone when the membrane-proximal layer of the SNARE was disrupted by mutation (Hernandez et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Extended close contacts were induced by SNAREs alone when the membrane-proximal layer of the SNARE was disrupted by mutation.
source: Interestingly, similar extended close contacts were induced between liposomes by denatured Munc18 (Xu et al., 2011), and by SNAREs alone when the membrane-proximal layer of the SNARE was disrupted by mutation (Hernandez et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Hemifusion diaphragms and extended close contacts observed approximately 35 s after Ca2+-injection are expected to be part of delayed fusion pathways.
source: Since we observed these hemifusion diaphragms and extended close contacts by cryo-EM imaging approximately 35 s after Ca2+-injection, such interfaces are expected to be part of 'slow', that is, delayed fusion pathways.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of observations relative to fusion kinetics.

claim: Some fusion occurred after Ca2+-addition, shifting the diameter distribution of vesicles towards larger vesicles.
source: As expected from our single-vesicle microscopy fusion experiments with identical vesicle preparations, some fusion occurred after Ca2+-addition, shifting the diameter distribution of vesicles observed in the cryo-EM images towards larger vesicles than before Ca2+ addition, that is, there are fewer small vesicles and more larger vesicles than before Ca2+-addition (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cryo-EM images shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The mean diameter increased from 61.3 ± 18.6 (s.d.) nm to 65.1 ± 23.9 (s.d.) nm after Ca2+ addition.
source: The mean diameter increased from 61.3 ± 18.6 (s.d.) nm to 65.1 ± 23.9 (s.d.) nm (a significant increase with 97% confidence from a Student's t-test), corresponding to an increase of mean volume from 1.6 × 105 nm3 to 2.2 × 105 nm3.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cryo-EM images with statistical testing.

claim: The distribution of vesicle interfaces changed after Ca2+ addition: the percentage of point contacts decreased from 55% to 40%.
source: Moreover, the distribution of vesicle interfaces changed after Ca2+ addition (Figure 2H): the percentage of point contacts decreased from 55% to 40%, the percentage of hemifused diaphragms increased from 45% to 49%, and the percentage of extended interfaces jumped from zero to 11%.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cryo-EM images shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The percentage of hemifused diaphragms increased from 45% to 49% after Ca2+ addition.
source: Moreover, the distribution of vesicle interfaces changed after Ca2+ addition (Figure 2H): the percentage of point contacts decreased from 55% to 40%, the percentage of hemifused diaphragms increased from 45% to 49%, and the percentage of extended interfaces jumped from zero to 11%.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cryo-EM images shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The percentage of extended interfaces jumped from zero to 11% after Ca2+ addition.
source: Moreover, the distribution of vesicle interfaces changed after Ca2+ addition (Figure 2H): the percentage of point contacts decreased from 55% to 40%, the percentage of hemifused diaphragms increased from 45% to 49%, and the percentage of extended interfaces jumped from zero to 11%.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cryo-EM images shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The cryo-EM images of most point contacts indicated that membranes are close to each other at the tip of the contact but not forming a membrane stalk.
source: The cryo-EM images of most point contacts indicated that membranes are close to each other at the tip of the contact but not forming a membrane stalk (an hourglass shaped connection between two bilayers that involves the merger of outer leaflets) since the observed minimal separation between membranes (ranging from 4.9 to 2.3 nm) was larger than the critical distance for membrane stalk formation (0.9 nm) (Aeffner et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on analysis of cryo-EM images with comparison to a critical distance from cited literature.

claim: A similar membrane apposition between liposomes could be induced by the soluble C2AB domain of synaptotagmin 1 and Ca2+, but without SNAREs.
source: Interestingly, a similar membrane apposition between liposomes could be induced by the soluble C2AB domain of synaptotagmin 1 and Ca2+, but without SNAREs (Araç et al., 2006), as well as with SNAREs alone (Hernandez et al., 2012); in this context it has been suggested that synaptotagmin may act as a distance regulator (van den Bogaart et al., 2011b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It has been suggested that synaptotagmin may act as a distance regulator.
source: in this context it has been suggested that synaptotagmin may act as a distance regulator (van den Bogaart et al., 2011b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The point contact is the only interface type where the proteins would be close to a putative transitory stalk to initiate fusion.
source: The point contact is a special case since it is the only interface type where the proteins would be close to a putative transitory stalk to initiate fusion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the geometry of the observed interfaces and protein sizes.

claim: The fraction of point contacts decreased upon Ca2+ addition.
source: Indeed, as mentioned above, quantitative analysis of all cryo-EM images revealed that the fraction of point contacts decreased upon Ca2+ addition (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cryo-EM images shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Some of the initial point contacts are the likely starting point for immediate fusion upon Ca2+ injection.
source: Inspired by this relative decrease after addition of Ca2+, we hypothesized that some of these initial point contacts are the likely starting point for immediate fusion upon Ca2+ injection; those that did not fuse might be ready to undergo fusion during subsequent pulses.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed decrease in point contacts after Ca2+ addition.

claim: No significant lipid fluorescence intensity changes were observed during the incubation period for all instances of immediate fusion events.
source: Remarkably, no significant lipid fluorescence intensity changes (i.e., changes larger than the noise level) were observed during the incubation period for 'all' instances of immediate fusion events (Figure 4A), in other words, these events did not start from a hemifused state.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Ca2+-triggered content mixing rarely occurred during the observation period of 50 s when starting from a stable hemifused state.
source: In contrast, Ca2+-triggered content mixing rarely occurred during the observation period of 50 s when starting from a stable hemifused state (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 4B.

claim: All immediate Ca2+-triggered fusion events must start from point contacts that are not hemifused.
source: Since cryo-EM imaging of the membrane interfaces prior to Ca2+-addition indicated that there were only two classes, point contacts and hemifusion diaphragms, it follows that all immediate Ca2+-triggered fusion events must start from point contacts that are not hemifused.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the combination of cryo-EM and fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: The position of synaptotagmin 1 in the models would enable Ca2+-triggered membrane juxtaposition.
source: For example, the position of synaptotagmin 1 in our models would enable Ca2+-triggered membrane juxtaposition (Araç et al., 2006) and membrane bending (Hui et al., 2009; McMahon et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a speculation based on structural models with citations to prior work on synaptotagmin function.

claim: Membrane bending or buckling could destabilize the membrane, and in conjunction with full zippering of the SNARE complex, lead to fusion pore opening.
source: Membrane bending or buckling could in turn destabilize the membrane, and in conjunction with full zippering of the SNARE complex, lead to fusion pore opening.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism for how fusion might occur.

claim: The content mixing histogram showed more pronounced short-time scale content mixing upon Ca2+ injection in the presence of complexin than in its absence.
source: Strikingly, the content mixing histogram showed more pronounced short-time scale content mixing upon Ca2+ injection than in the absence of complexin (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The content mixing histogram in the presence of complexin could be fitted to a biphasic exponential decay function where the fast fraction with a time constant of 0.36 s accounts for 68% of all events.
source: Indeed, the content mixing histogram in the presence of complexin could be fitted to a biphasic exponential decay function where the fast fraction with a time constant of 0.36 s accounts for 68% of all events.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At lower Ca2+ concentration (250 μM), the effect of complexin on the fusion probability time trace became even more pronounced with 90% in the fast fraction.
source: At lower Ca2+ concentration (250 μM), the effect of complexin on the fusion probability time trace became even more pronounced (Figure 6B) with 90% in the fast fraction.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In the absence of complexin, the fusion probability time trace was best fit to a single exponential decay function with a time constant of 3 s.
source: In contrast, the fusion probability time trace was best fit to a single exponential decay function with a time constant of 3 s in the absence of complexin, which is a significant difference to the content mixing histogram in the presence of complexin.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The immediate fusion pathway starts from a hemifusion-free point contact and proceeds to full fusion without discernible intermediates on the 100-ms time scale.
source: It starts from a hemifusion-free point contact and proceeds to full fusion without discernible intermediates on the 100-ms time scale.
evidence: This is based on the combination of cryo-EM and single vesicle-vesicle microscopy data.

claim: All instances of immediate fusion events upon Ca2+-triggering started from interacting membranes that were not hemifused.
source: We found that all instances of immediate fusion events upon Ca2+-triggering started from interacting membranes that were not hemifused.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from single vesicle-vesicle microscopy shown in Figure 4A.

claim: It is possible that the immediate pathway proceeds from point contact to fusion pore via a transient stalk with a lifetime faster than 100 ms.
source: It is of course possible that this immediate pathway proceeds from point contact to fusion pore via a transient stalk, however, the lifetime of such a transient stalk would have to be faster than the 100-ms time resolution of our instrument.
evidence: This is a speculation about a possible intermediate that cannot be resolved by the current technique.

claim: The experiments definitely rule out the existence of a stable hemifusion intermediate for fast Ca2+-triggered fusion.
source: Our experiments definitely rule out the existence of a stable hemifusion intermediate for fast Ca2+-triggered fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing no hemifusion before immediate fusion events.

claim: Complexin significantly increased the number of immediate fusion events that occur right upon Ca2+-injection.
source: Specifically, we observed that complexin significantly increased the number of immediate fusion events that occur right upon Ca2+-injection (Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Complexin suppresses the emergence of long-lived hemifusion intermediates, effectively leading to a higher probability of immediate fusion upon Ca2+-triggering.
source: Thus, complexin suppresses the emergence of long-lived hemifusion intermediates, effectively leading to a higher probability of immediate fusion upon Ca2+-triggering.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations of complexin's effects.

claim: Complexin was recently found to prevent spontaneous fusion in the absence of Ca2+ in another model system with proteoliposomes.
source: Moreover, complexin was recently found to prevent spontaneous fusion in the absence of Ca2+ in another model system with proteoliposomes (Malsam et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: There are two distinct N-terminal sequence elements that are required for complexin's activating role in vivo, one of which (the accessory α-helix) clamps SNARE complexes.
source: There are two distinct N-terminal sequence elements that required for complexin's activating role in vivo, one of which (the accessory α-helix) clamps SNARE complexes (Krishnakumar et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Complexin's activating function may be explained by imposing geometric restraints on trans SNARE complexes through inter-SNARE complex interactions, thereby possibly preventing the formation of long-lived hemifusion intermediates upon Ca2+-triggering.
source: Our results suggest a possible explanation activating function of complexin by imposing geometric restraints on trans SNARE complexes through inter-SNARE complex interactions (Kümmel et al., 2011), and thereby possibly preventing the formation of long-lived hemifusion intermediates upon Ca2+-triggering.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism based on the experimental results and cited structural work.

claim: SNAREs alone can produce a variety of spontaneous fusion pathways on the minute time scale at elevated temperature (30°C), including point contacts, extended close contacts, and hemifusion diaphragms.
source: A recent study showed that SNAREs alone can produce a variety of spontaneous (i.e., without Ca2+-triggering) fusion pathways on the minute time scale at elevated temperature (30°C) (Hernandez et al., 2012), including point contacts, as well as extended close contacts, and hemifusion diagrams.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Biological membranes are poised to undergo fusion via a number of different pathways once they are brought into close proximity by the action of SNAREs.
source: Thus, biological membranes are poised to undergo fusion via a number of different pathways once they are brought into close proximity by the action of SNAREs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the variety of pathways observed experimentally.

claim: Factors such as complexin may have evolved to select the immediate pathway out of all possible pathways.
source: Factors such as complexin may have evolved to select this immediate pathway out of all possible pathways, and may have offered a distinct advantage for fast Ca2+-evoked release and efficient communication between neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Complexin had little effect on the lipid mixing histogram upon 500 μM Ca2+ injection.
source: As a further demonstration of this principle, complexin had little effect on the lipid mixing histogram upon 500 μM Ca2+ injection (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Complexin had a large effect on the content mixing histograms at 500 μM Ca2+.
source: In marked contrast, complexin had a large effect on the corresponding content mixing histograms (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At 250 μM Ca2+, the effect of complexin is more pronounced on the content mixing histogram compared to the lipid mixing histogram.
source: Likewise, at 250 μM Ca2 the effect of complexin is more pronounced on the content mixing histogram compared to the lipid mixing histogram (compare Figures 6b and 8b).
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data shown in Figures 6B and 8B.

claim: The large difference in complexin-induced lipid mixing and content mixing effects greatly amplifies previous observations for biological membrane fusion.
source: This large difference in complexin-induced lipid mixing and content mixing effects greatly amplifies previous observations for biological membrane fusion (Bowen et al., 2004; Jun and Wickner, 2007; Floyd et al., 2008; Chan et al., 2009; Kyoung et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work supported by citations.

claim: It is essential that biological fusion experiments monitor a quantity that is directly related to content mixing in order to distinguish between different membrane states.
source: It is thus essential that biological fusion experiments monitor a quantity that is directly related to content mixing in order to distinguish between different membrane states, such as docking, hemifusion, and full fusion.
evidence: This is a methodological conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Before Ca2+ addition, the majority (55%) of interacting vesicles formed point contacts.
source: Before Ca2+ addition, the majority (55%) of interacting vesicles formed point contacts, while the remaining vesicle interfaces consisted of hemifusion diaphragms (Figure 2H) with SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of cryo-EM images shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Only a small fraction of vesicles underwent spontaneous (complete) fusion during the incubation period.
source: Only a small fraction of vesicles underwent spontaneous (complete) fusion during the incubation period.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations during the incubation period.

claim: Starting from hemifused vesicles, little complete fusion was observed upon Ca2+-injection.
source: Starting from hemifused vesicles, little complete fusion was observed upon Ca2+-injection (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Starting from point contacts, a heterogeneous network of both immediate and delayed fusion pathways was observed upon Ca2+ injection.
source: In contrast, starting from point contacts, we observed a heterogeneous network of both immediate and delayed fusion pathways upon Ca2+ injection (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations summarized in Figure 7.

claim: The very minimal system of just SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1 exhibited Ca2+ triggered activity, including instances of immediate fusion.
source: It is remarkable that the very minimal system of just SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1 exhibited Ca2+ triggered activity, including instances of immediate fusion (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The delayed fusion pathways proceeded on a second to minute time scale via long-lived extended contact or hemifusion intermediates.
source: The delayed fusion pathways proceeded on a second to minute time scale via long-lived extended contact or hemifusion intermediates (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations summarized in Figure 7.

claim: The pathway for immediate Ca2+-triggered fusion starts from a hemifusion-free point contact and proceeds to full fusion without discernible intermediates on the 100-ms time scale.
source: Our experiments revealed the pathway for immediate Ca2+-triggered fusion by synaptic proteins (Figure 7). It starts from a hemifusion-free point contact and proceeds to full fusion without discernible intermediates on the 100-ms time scale.
evidence: This is based on the combination of experimental data from single vesicle-vesicle microscopy and cryo-EM.

claim: Complexin favors the immediate fusion pathway upon Ca2+ triggering, correlating well with complexin's activating role in vivo for synchronous release upon an action potential.
source: We confirmed this hypothesis by observing that complexin (in combination with SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1) favors this immediate fusion pathway upon Ca2+ triggering, a result that correlates well with complexin's activating role in vivo for synchronous release upon an action potential (Maximov et al., 2009).
evidence: This is based on experimental data with citation to prior in vivo work.

claim: Optical tweezer pulling experiments revealed a partially folded intermediate state of the SNARE complex under external force conditions.
source: Optical tweezer pulling experiments recently revealed a partially folded intermediate state of the SNARE complex under external force conditions (Gao et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The partially folded intermediate state of the SNARE complex likely facilitates the metastable state of interacting and largely unfused vesicles during the incubation stage at zero Ca2+.
source: This intermediate state likely facilitates the metastable state of interacting and largely unfused vesicles during the incubation stage at zero Ca2+ at ambient (25°C) temperature that is the starting point for our system.
evidence: This is an inference connecting prior work on SNARE intermediates to the experimental system.

claim: The incubation period at zero Ca2+ should reduce cis-interactions between the C2 domains of synaptotagmin to its own membrane that otherwise might prevent proper trans-interactions with acceptor vesicles.
source: On a more technical note, the incubation period at zero Ca2+ should reduce cis-interactions between the C2 domains of synaptotagmin to its own membrane that otherwise might prevent proper trans-interactions with acceptor vesicles in assays that use a constant non-zero Ca2+-concentration (Vennekate et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference about the experimental design with citation to prior work on synaptotagmin interactions.

claim: The addition of other synaptic factors may further increase the Ca2+ sensitivity of the system.
source: This Ca2+-range is reasonably close to the physiological concentration range (starting at 10 μM and saturating at several 100 μM) (Heidelberger et al., 1994), although it is conceivable that the addition of other synaptic factors will further increase the Ca2+ sensitivity.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential improvements to the system.

claim: The synaptobrevin and syntaxin protein to lipid ratio was 1:200.
source: The synaptobrevin and syntaxin protein to lipid ratio was 1:200; the synaptotagmin 1 to synaptobrevin molar ratio was 1:4.6, consistent with observations of purified synaptic vesicles (Takamori et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The synaptotagmin 1 to synaptobrevin molar ratio was 1:4.6, consistent with observations of purified synaptic vesicles.
source: the synaptotagmin 1 to synaptobrevin molar ratio was 1:4.6, consistent with observations of purified synaptic vesicles (Takamori et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design with citation to prior work on synaptic vesicle composition.

claim: 3.5 mol% phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) was added to the acceptor vesicles only.
source: 3.5 mol% phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) was added to the acceptor vesicles only; this concentration is within the range of that observed in the plasma membrane of PC12 cells (van den Bogaart et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design with citation to prior work on PIP2 concentrations.
